info.title: kling/videos-lip-sync
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "kling/videos-lip-sync", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Generate lip-sync for a video_id or video_url. Use text2video with text and voice_id, or audio2video with an audio_file or audio_url.

callback_url.description: The callback notification address. Server will notify when the task status changes.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Kling v1 VIDEO models: the terminal `GET /v1/videos/{operation}/{id}` task-query document, forwarded unchanged. Every Kling v1 operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `routerresult/classification.go` records `/v1/videos/text2video`, `/v1/videos/image2video`, `/v1/videos/omni-video`, `/v1/videos/avatar/image2video`, `/v1/videos/lip-sync` and `/v1/videos/video-extend` as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll`, each polled on `<submit path>/:id` — and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `{code, message, request_id, data.task_id}` handle the underlying `/proxy/kling/*` submit answers with.
The generated video's download URL is at `data.task_result.videos[].url`. Read the ELEMENT field, not the `videos` container: `KlingVideoResult` is `{id, url, watermark_url, duration}`, so a one-element list carrying an id and a duration and no URL is a non-empty array holding nothing playable. `data.task_result.videos[].watermark_url` is the same asset under Kling's hotlink-protection form and counts as a result; `routerpollstate.classifyKling` draws exactly that line, and a `succeed` carrying neither is `success_without_output` rather than a finished generation.
`data.task_status` is Kling's own four-value vocabulary — `submitted`, `processing`, `succeed`, `failed` — and the terminal success spells it `succeed`, NOT `succeeded`. The `kling/kling-3.0-turbo` sibling (`KlingV2RouterOutput`) says `succeeded` and carries an entirely different document; the two vocabularies are deliberately not folded together.
Six operations share this component because they share this document, and the ids are grouped by operation in the list above: text2video is the family's primary, so `kling/kling-v1-5` and `kling/kling-v2-1` — the two ids text2video's allowlist does not admit — resolve onto image2video, and `kling/kling-v3-omni` and `kling/kling-video-o1` resolve onto omni-video. The last three ids are route-slug models — `kling/videos-avatar-image2video`, `kling/videos-lip-sync` and `kling/videos-video-extend` — each the only id on its own operation. Their documents are typed separately in the v1 contract (`KlingAvatarResponse`, `KlingLipSyncResponse`, `KlingVideoExtendResponse`) but describe the same envelope and the same `data.task_result.videos[]` leaf, which is why they are documented here rather than as three near-identical components. Two of them carry a NARROWER envelope than the eleven generation ids: `KlingLipSyncResponse` and `KlingVideoExtendResponse` declare no `task_status_msg`, `watermark_info` or `final_unit_deduction`, so treat those three FIELDS as absent for those two models even though this schema admits them. Each of the three route-slug ids publishes its own example, on its own model page; the eleven generation-id pages carry the shared text2video one.

KlingAudioUploadType.description: Method of Transmitting Audio Files for Lip-Sync. Required when mode is audio2video.

audio_file.description: Local Path of Audio File. Supported formats: .mp3/.wav/.m4a/.aac, maximum file size of 5MB. Base64 code.

audio_url.description: Audio File Download URL. Supported formats: .mp3/.wav/.m4a/.aac, maximum file size of 5MB.

text.description: Text Content for Lip-Sync Video Generation. Required when mode is text2video. Maximum length is 120 characters.

video_id.description: The ID of the video generated by Kling AI. Only supports 5-second and 10-second videos generated within the last 30 days.

video_url.description: Get link for uploaded video. Video files support .mp4/.mov, file size does not exceed 100MB, video length between 2-10s.

voice_id.description: Voice ID. Required when mode is text2video. The system offers a variety of voice options to choose from.

voice_speed.description: Speech Rate. Valid range: 0.8~2.0, accurate to one decimal place.

KlingLipSyncMode.description: Video Generation Mode. text2video: Text-to-video generation mode; audio2video: Audio-to-video generation mode

KlingLipSyncVoiceLanguage.description: The voice language corresponds to the Voice ID.

created_at.description: Task creation time, Unix timestamp in milliseconds

task_status_msg.description: Task status information, displaying the failure reason when the task fails

updated_at.description: Task update time, Unix timestamp in milliseconds

watermark_url.description: URL for generated video with watermark, hotlink protection format
